session.question: How do sustainable technologies and environmantal management relate in the context of Industry 4.0 and SDGs, and what did the study find about enterprises preference for environmental aspects in business management?
session.answer:
Sustainable technologies in Industry 4.0 are presented as enablers of sustainability across manufacturing and logistics, particularly when aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). In this context, clean energy, green logistics, reverse logistics, and digital technologies such as IoT, cloud computing, big data, AI, blockchain, and digital twins support more sustainable production, supply chain management, and ESG (environmental, social, and governance) performance assessment. Environmental management is therefore closely linked to sustainability-oriented production and logistics practices, including renewable energy use, waste separation and recycling, environmental certification, employee training, and CO2 reduction. (richnak2022impactandpotential chunk 1, chauhan2022digitalizationofsupply chunk 1)

The study of 105 Slovak enterprises found that more than 82% were implementing SDGs, and over 70% preferred environmental aspects in business management. This indicates a strong managerial orientation toward environmental sustainability within industrial enterprises, consistent with the broader Industry 4.0–SDG framework. (richnak2022impactandpotential chunk 1)

session.context:
pqac-2f04309d: The article examines sustainable technologies in manufacturing and logistics in connection with Industry 4.0 and Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). It reports that sustainable technologies such as clean energy, green logistics, and reverse logistics support industry development and future growth when combined with Industry 4.0 innovations. In the study of 105 Slovak enterprises, more than 82% were implementing SDGs, and over 70% preferred environmental aspects in business management. The authors found a significant relationship between environmental management and sustainability in production and logistics, including renewable energy use, waste separation and recycling, environmental certification, employee training, and CO2 reduction.
From Patrik Richnák and Helena Fidlerová. Impact and potential of sustainable development goals in dimension of the technological revolution industry 4.0 within the analysis of industrial enterprises. Energies, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/en15103697, doi:10.3390/en15103697.

pqac-db748c6d: The excerpt discusses digitalization of supply chain management through Industry 4.0 technologies in a sustainable perspective. It states that supply chain management must incorporate sustainability to support responsible consumption and production (SDG 11), and that Industry 4.0 technologies such as IoT, cloud computing, big data, AI, blockchain, and digital twins can help achieve sustainable SCM. The paper emphasizes using these technologies to assess sustainability performance through environmental, social, and governance (ESG) metrics. It also notes that prior work is limited, especially in developing countries, and focuses mostly on case studies and operational/economic aspects.
From Sanjay Chauhan, Rajesh Singh, Anita Gehlot, Shaik Vaseem Akram, Bhekisipho Twala, and Neeraj Priyadarshi. Digitalization of supply chain management with industry 4.0 enabling technologies: a sustainable perspective. Processes, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/pr11010096, doi:10.3390/pr11010096.

pqac-ec96f970: The excerpt explains that Industry 4.0 digital technologies (AI, cloud computing, robotics, big data analytics, and blockchain) are studied as strategic resources that can support environmental and social sustainability in manufacturing multinational enterprises. The study found that digital technologies positively contribute to environmental and social sustainability, helping drive greener manufacturing and supporting the UN Sustainable Development Goals. However, European manufacturing MNEs still had low overall implementation of these technologies. The abstract also notes that the contribution of each technology differs, so firms can prioritize investments based on expected returns. It does not explicitly state a preference for environmental aspects in business management.
From João J. Ferreira, Jo�ão M. Lopes, Sofia Gomes, and Hussain Gulzar Rammal. Industry 4.0 implementation: environmental and social sustainability in manufacturing multinational enterprises. Journal of Cleaner Production, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jclepro.2023.136841, doi:10.1016/j.jclepro.2023.136841.

pqac-36d9030b: The article frames Industry 4.0 technologies (e.g., blockchain, Big Data, IoT, cloud computing, AI, additive manufacturing) as part of the broader response to climate change and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), emphasizing their potential role in transforming enterprise risk management toward sustainability. It notes that COVID-19 accelerated digital transformation, possibly including sustainability risk management. The study surveyed managers and found that the number of Industry 4.0 technologies used in sustainability risk management did not significantly affect financial performance or financial risk management ability. The excerpt does not explicitly report a preference for environmental aspects in business management, but it highlights the integration of sustainable development strategies with long-term risk management.
From Jolanta Turek, Barbara Ocicka, Waldemar Rogowski, and Bartłomiej Jefmański. The role of industry 4.0 technologies in driving the financial importance of sustainability risk management. Equilibrium Quarterly Journal of Economics and Economic Policy, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.24136/eq.2023.032, doi:10.24136/eq.2023.032.

pqac-5e1ee2da: The excerpt describes a literature review on how Industry 4.0 technologies such as AI, IoT, big data, and machine learning can improve environmental sustainability in manufacturing and other industries. It says these technologies support sustainable manufacturing, reduce resource consumption, improve efficiency, and positively affect environmental aspects across production, supply chains, and delivery chains. However, the excerpt does not mention Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) directly, nor does it discuss enterprises’ preference for environmental aspects in business management. It only generally frames Industry 4.0 as contributing to a more sustainable environment.
From Mohd Javaid, Abid Haleem, Ravi Pratap Singh, Rajiv Suman, and Ernesto D.R. Santibañez González. Understanding the adoption of industry 4.0 technologies in improving environmental sustainability. Sustainable Operations and Computers, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.susoc.2022.01.008, doi:10.1016/j.susoc.2022.01.008.
